purpose: Conceptual research illustrations, not physical layouts or measured results

prompts.system: Scientific educational diagram for a professor's PowerPoint, wide landscape 16:9, pure white background, restrained flat vector-like academic line art, dark navy outlines, muted teal computation, pale gold memory, Times New Roman labels LARGE, generous whitespace. Draw exactly ONE external DRAM rectangle far left labelled 'DRAM', linked bidirectionally only to the top-left chiplet c0 of a two-by-two rectangular mesh of four identical compute chiplets. Chiplets labelled c0,c1,c2,c3 in reading order, mesh has four orthogonal neighbor connections, no diagonal links. Each chiplet has one simple small internal block 'GB' and one 'PE'. On one neighbor link show a teal arrow labelled 'GB peer transfer'. Below DRAM arrow label 'DMA'. Under mesh label 'Compute chiplets'. The four chips are an EXAMPLE, not optimal design. No second DRAM, no memory chiplet, no central crossbar, no CPU, no 3D photorealism, no tiny annotations, no title, no numerical performance claims. Main diagram fills center 85 percent of image with 8 percent white margins.
prompts.hierarchy: Scientific educational diagram for an academic slide, WIDE 16:9 pure white background, sparse clean schematic, dark navy outlines, muted teal and pale gold highlights, very LARGE Times New Roman text, generous whitespace. Exact data path five blocks horizontally: 'DRAM', 'GB', 'LB', 'RF', 'PE'. Bidirectional arrows connect consecutive blocks. Distinguish chip boundary: DRAM outside at left; GB,LB,RF,PE inside a simple thin boundary labelled 'One compute chiplet'. Below LB draw ONE separate block 'ACC' with a vertical bidirectional connection directly to LB only. Below RF draw ONE separate block 'FP32 Vector' with a vertical bidirectional connection directly to RF only. Internal blocks label two lines: 'GB' and '256 KiB'; 'LB' and '20 KiB'; 'RF' and '1.5 KiB'; 'PE' and '16 x 16'; 'ACC' and '64 KiB'. External DRAM label no capacity. Visual concept is memory hierarchy and separate SRAM accumulator, NOT ACC inline in the operand chain. No duplicated labels, no additional objects, no second DRAM, no charts, no slide title, no prose, NO gradients, no shadows. Labels and arrows entirely inside margins.
prompts.tiling: Scientific educational concept diagram for professor presentation, wide 16:9 white background. Flat technical isometric cubes outlined navy, muted teal and pale gold tile regions, Times New Roman labels LARGE and minimal. Show one 3D OUTPUT activation tensor on left split exactly 2 by 2 by 2, meaning eight equal blocks. Three clearly distinct outside dimension labels 'H = 16', 'W = 16', 'Cout = 32'. Cube boundaries must follow the three independent axes. Center a single rightward navy arrow. On right show exactly eight separate equal cubes arranged two rows of four, labelled collectively '8 output tiles', with one enlarged representative tile next to them labelled '8 x 8 x 16'. Keep Cout axis distinct from the two spatial axes. No CNN kernel, no equation, no performance claim, no extra numbers, no title, no Chinese text, no gradients, no long text. Very large whitespace so concept can be understood in 5 seconds. Schematic only, not real tensor measurements.
prompts.reuse: Scientific educational diagram on pure white 16:9 background, academic line-art with navy outlines muted teal and pale gold, very LARGE Times New Roman labels. Show ONE weight block 'W' at left, arrow into one register file 'RF'. Show RF attached above one 'PE Array' compute block. Along bottom left, a stream of three input activation tiles labelled 'A1', 'A2', 'A3' enters same PE Array sequentially. PE Array has one arrow exiting right to three output tiles labelled 'Y1', 'Y2', 'Y3'. Weight W held in RF stays fixed while the A tiles change. Label above RF 'Weight reuse', and near input stream 'Next input tile'. Only one load arrow from W into RF, do not draw repeated reload arrows or a hidden external memory. No numeric performance result, no slide title, no Chinese, no photorealism, no detailed circuitry, no tiny text. Use exact topology; output three tiles total; one RF and one PE Array total.
prompts.joint: Scientific educational joint-action diagram for a professor's slide, white 16:9 canvas, flat academic line art, navy outlines teal compute and pale gold evaluation, LARGE Times New Roman labels, sparse whitespace. Left shows two dependent operators: square 'A' on chip labelled 'c0', connected by a long horizontal arrow to square 'B' on a separate chip labelled 'c3'. Above left label 'Current design'. Center is one large arrow labelled 'Joint action'. Right shows exactly one chip labelled 'c1' containing operator squares 'A' and 'B' linked internally. Above right label 'New complete design'. From the completed right chip ONE arrow goes down to a single pale gold box labelled 'Environment'. Label adjacent 'One evaluation'. The change is an EXAMPLE of changing BOTH producer A and consumer B in one action. Do not draw two agent networks, intermediate PPA evaluation, loops, or external DRAM. Do not claim objective improvement. No small text, no title, no 3D rendering.
prompts.update: Scientific educational schematic for professor PowerPoint, very wide 16:9 pure white canvas, restrained flat academic line art dark navy, teal and pale gold, very large Times New Roman labels with minimal text. Draw two clearly separated horizontal zones. TOP zone labelled 'Within one episode': three pairs of small blocks from left to right: 'Action 1' then 'Feedback 1', 'Action 2' then 'Feedback 2', 'Action T' then 'Feedback T', linked sequentially by simple arrows. Text underneath this top path 'Same policy parameters'. BOTTOM centered zone is a single large pale gold block labelled 'One REINFORCE update'. A thin arrow goes from the completed top path at far right downward into the bottom update block. A final arrow from the update block to one box at bottom left labelled 'Next episode'. Labels may wrap to two lines for clean spacing. The update happens only AFTER completing the entire episode, not after each action. Do not label training as PPO, no critic, no prediction of PPA, no chart, no equations, no title, no small annotations, do not draw additional policy updates. Use generous whitespace and a professional scientific paper illustration style.
